To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the insulin/IGF1 and the AMPK/mTOR pathways are central to the control of metabolic homeostatic processes and are involved in the regulation of ageing.
the growth factor, energy and nutrients sensing signalling pathways regulate cellular and organismal metabolism, and their deregulation contributes to the ageing process.

(i) the IGF-1/insulin signalling pathway is a central regulator of ageing and metabolic homeostasis, and (ii) that the mTOR pathway is a key regulator of nutrient sensing and energy balance, and a major player in the ageing process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of growth factor, energy and nutrientsensing signalling pathways in metabolic homeostasis and the ageing phenotype.
the identification and validation of the mechanisms that regulate metabolic ageing and the development of novel therapeutic strategies for metabolic diseases.
the study of the molecular mechanisms that regulate metabolic homeostasis and how they are altered with ageing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field is far from mature and there is still a long way to go before we can fully understand the mechanisms that regulate the ageing phenotype and the role of metabolism in ageing.
the ageing process is the sum total of the effects of multiple genes and pathways, and it is the interplay among them that determines the rate of ageing and the onset of age-related diseases.
ageing is a complex process that involves the coordinated regulation of multiple signalling pathways and cellular functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified and characterized the signalling pathways involved in the metabolic deterioration of ageing.
the insulin/insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1)/insulin receptor substrate-2/PI-3K/ Akt/mTORC1 pathway plays a key role in the regulation of ageing and metabolic homeostasis.

the insulin/insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-1 signalling (IIS) pathway, the nutrient sensing mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway and the energy sensing adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) pathway are the main signalling pathways implicated in metabolic ageing and the respective pharmacological interventions have shown beneficial metabolic effects in model organisms and humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of pharmacological agents targeting multiple pathways and processes is likely to be more effective than single agents.
the signalling pathways regulating growth, energy and nutrient homeostasis are key determinants of metabolic ageing.
the insulin/IGF-1 signalling (IIS) and the mTOR signalling pathways are central to metabolic ageing.
